articles.hed: Week 2 Home Opener: 59-Point Bears Host Flores’ Vikings
articles.deck: Both 1–0. Johnson’s attack vs. Minnesota’s blitz package at Soldier Field Sunday 12 PM CT.
articles.body: Chicago’s franchise-opener 59–37 demolition of Carolina still echoes — Caleb Williams, Swift, and Monangai combined for a historic scoring day. Minnesota answered Week 1 with a 39–22 win over Green Bay and four second-half sacks. Sunday at Soldier Field (Fox, noon CT) is Ben Johnson’s high-flying offense against Brian Flores’ deceptive pressure. Odds lean Bears by about 4½. Carry that tempo into the Opening Bell — then skim the board.

items.hed: The Clear Window Is the Working Hour
items.body: Hermetic timing lore prized the lucida — the bright interval before the next weather of the soul. Friday morning’s partly sunny stretch is that window: charge and body while the radar is quiet, then let the overnight storms do their outer work. Mystics did not wait for forever-clear skies; they worked the opening that arrived.

items.hed: Gnosis Favors the Named Next Step
items.body: Gnostic texts treat forgetfulness as the real prison — not the world, but losing the thread of what you already know. Name today’s sequence out loud: breath, plank, security skim, then the rest. Unnamed urgency dilutes will; a named next step is already half done.

items.hed: Sigils Exhaust What the Day Did Not
items.body: Esoteric practice often ends the day by discharging leftover charge — not adding more. The optional 9:30 Sigil is that valve: if thoughts are still floating, give them a mark and close the book. Forbidden knowledge, stripped of theater, is often just clean endings so tomorrow can open clean.

items.hed: Anthropic: Claude now leads 26% of work building its next models
items.body: Anthropic said Claude “leads” about 26% of internal AI R&D (up from 1% in March), with human–AI collaboration on more than 90% of research as of August. Roughly 30,000 agents work on its main platform at once; every action is screened, and about 1 in 47,000 decisions was blocked in August.

items.hed: Judge seals Apple–SpaceXAI settlement; OpenAI kept out of the terms
items.body: After X Corp and SpaceXAI dismissed antitrust claims against Apple, OpenAI asked to see the settlement. Judge Pittman reviewed it and denied disclosure, citing the federal policy favoring confidential settlements. Claims against OpenAI remain active.

items.hed: iOS 27 code shows Siri AI can be swapped for Claude or ChatGPT
items.body: Private Model Delegation and Inference Provider hooks in iOS 27 / macOS Golden Gate betas can run Claude as a Siri extension or replace Siri’s server model with ChatGPT — demos exist, but the features are not enabled for regular users yet.

items.hed: X Corp and SpaceXAI drop Apple claims; OpenAI case continues
items.body: A Sept. 14 motion dismissed antitrust claims against Apple with prejudice after the parties said they “resolved their claims.” Every claim against the OpenAI entities stays; trial is set for January 2027.

items.hed: Raptors close to Kawhi Leonard contract extension
items.body: Multiple reports say Toronto and Kawhi are nearing an extension after Monday’s trade from the Clippers. He is eligible for up to two years and $126M; talks accelerated once the NBA’s cap probe cleared the deal.

items.hed: Raptors finalize Kawhi trade: Ingram, Dick, and picks to L.A.
items.body: Toronto officially acquired Leonard on Sept. 15 for Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two first-round picks, a first-round swap, and two seconds. Media day expected late September; camp follows in Quebec.

items.hed: Extension talks advanced — money and minutes are the real levers
items.body: Kawhi makes $50.3M this season in the final year of his deal. Insiders expect a two-year pact below the absolute max as Toronto balances impact against injury history and rest nights.

items.hed: Bears host Vikings: Johnson’s 59-point attack vs. Flores’ pressure
items.body: Both teams are 1–0. Chicago dropped 59 on Carolina; Minnesota sacked Love four times in the second half of a 39–22 win over Green Bay. Sunday noon CT at Soldier Field on Fox — Bears favored by about 4½.

items.hed: Week 2 game center locked: Minnesota at Chicago, Sep 20
items.body: Official Vikings game center lists Sunday Sept. 20 at Soldier Field, 12:00 PM CDT. Both clubs enter 1–0; Hockenson and O’Connell already teed up the Bears matchup in midweek availability.

items.hed: Chiefs’ new-look ground game next test for Colts on SNF
items.body: Kansas City rides Kenneth Walker III’s 173-yard debut and Mahomes’ return into Sunday Night Football vs. Indianapolis. Preview focus: KC’s refreshed rush attack against a Colts front that struggled with heavy backs in Week 1.

items.hed: Aspinall steps back from podcasting after vacating HW title
items.body: Days after relinquishing the UFC heavyweight belt amid ongoing eye issues, Tom Aspinall said he is pausing podcasting and social to focus on a medical return — hoped for early 2027. Ciryl Gane remains interim; no formal undisputed elevation yet.

items.hed: Masvidal floats boxing rumors after Aspinall’s title drop
items.body: Jorge Masvidal questioned whether vacating could be a path toward boxing, noting Eddie Hearn’s role as Aspinall’s manager. No bout or UFC release has been announced; Aspinall’s public line remains an MMA return when cleared.

openingBell.title: The Opening Bell

breathing.title: Box Breathing — 4 · 4 · 4 · 4

phases.label: INHALE
phases.cue: Draw in through the nose — even, quiet, full.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Stillness at the top. No strain. Own the pause.

phases.label: HOLD
phases.cue: Empty and steady. Reset the line.

breathing.close: Four rounds clears the static. Eyes open. Shoulders down. Body next. Then the rest of the board.

mindset.body: Dom does not wait for perfect forecasts to start. Fierce calm is Friday composure when the week still has unfinished boards: charge first, body second, security skim when ready, admin only after the morning has already won. One breath, one move, one clear next step. Competitors may arrive loud for Week 2; he arrives prepared. When pressure rises, he slows the breath, names the next action, and outlasts the noise. Today is not about proving anything. It is about banking Friday energy so Sunday’s Soldier Field and Monday’s portal have a clean operator behind them.

bodyOpener.title: 3-Minute Opener
bodyOpener.note: Friday: run this after Morning Charge — box breathing first, then the body. Clear skies now; storms later. Then news and the day.

moves.name: Push-ups
moves.body: Crisp reps, chest to floor. If you hit 30 early, hold high plank until the minute mark.

moves.name: Plank
moves.body: Elbows or hands. Ribs down, glutes on. Breathe slow.

moves.name: RipStick finisher
moves.body: Dom’s RipStick (RipRight): hold sticks at chest → inhale and pull apart as wide as possible → with bands open, exhale and push arms straight out while keeping them apart (dynamic isometrics / Push-Pulls). Smooth continuous reps for the remaining time. Optional: Front Clips / Back Clips if you want a second RipStick move.

grimoire.title: Grimoire
grimoire.hed: Prepare the Field Before You Build the House
grimoire.body: “Prepare your work outside; get everything ready for yourself in the field, and after that build your house.” (Proverbs 24:27) Solomon’s counsel is sequence: ready the ground before you raise the structure. Friday’s charge and body are the field work — security skim and Later / Admin are the house. Classical lore cast Solomon as one who ordered materials before the build. Order the morning the same way, so Soldier Field Sunday and Monday’s portal sit on prepared ground.
grimoire.practice: Finish Opening Bell and the 3-minute opener before any security skim or admin. Field first; house second.

techDemo.pick: SpaceXAI Amrita session — Grok Bot across four departments (GTM, engineering, marketing, admin)
techDemo.author: @0xGenAi

image.alt: Newsprint diagram — You/CoS hub routing to GTM, ENG, MKT, and ADMIN Grok Bot lanes

lesson.oneLiner: Stop one-chat everything. Assign four lanes — GTM, eng, marketing, admin — and let workers keep executing after you close the laptop.
beats: GTM lane: bots build and babysit sales pipelines so outreach doesn’t die when you step away.
Engineering lane: reproduce bugs with screenshots instead of dumping stack traces into one mega-thread.
Marketing lane: monitor campaigns continuously — alerts, not doomscrolling.
Admin lane: calendar, travel, expenses, inbox triage as dedicated workers, not side quests.
Amrita’s punchline: a free SpaceXAI training day beats a $500 “agent course” if you actually stand up the four lanes.
lesson.takeaway: Under a minute: pick one department today, name a worker, give it one recurring job — then watch the bookmark session for the other three.
